analysis: Examined the supplied base text (lines 1047-1611) and head text (lines 1-551) of ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift. The visible changes are in the memory-admission and eviction-feasibility helpers: reclaimableMemoryGb and reclaimableMemoryBytes gain a countingRetainedKVSegments parameter, and a new evictionCanReach wrapper is added. The patch also touches evictUntilAvailable, fastAdmissionReject, throwIfRetiring, and the load-error mapping around head lines 1555-1589. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the head text supplied ends at line 551. The changed head regions (1305-1589) are therefore not visible, so I could not verify them. The visible head section is the weight-hash capture, publish, and finalize logic plus the start of ensureModelLoaded. It appears to match the reusable-SSD fail-closed design in T-041: fresh cryptographic hashes are taken before and after the load, a mismatch aborts the load, and an unavailable hash disables SSD reuse and clears the registered hash. I saw no regression there. The admission and eviction changes are availability and memory-accounting logic. They relate to the T-016 and T-029 availability class and to T-010-style resource handling, not to a visible confidentiality or authorization boundary. Open questions: whether the new retained-KV-segment crediting (the full definition is not visible) can over-credit reclaimable memory and admit loads that later 503, and whether the release-before-load path interacts with the KV and SSD staging reservations in T-041. These need a pass over the full head diff, which is not supplied. No concrete security finding is supported by the visible evidence.
